event_description: Governor Baker Declares State of Emergency for Winter Storm Riley
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of low pressure rapidly intensified off the coast of Long Island on March 2nd, 2018. A large swath of tropical moisture was fed into the storm, resulting in a period of moderate to heavy precipitation throughout the day. The precipitation type was highly dependent on elevation, with lower elevations seeing a significant amount of rain mixing in with snow, while higher elevations saw mainly snow. Snowfall accumulations ranged from around three inches up to a foot over the higher terrain. The combination of snow and gusty winds resulted in scattered power outages.

event_description: Governor Healey Issues Emergency Declaration, Activates National Guard Ahead of Hurricane Lee
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal system brought a period of heavy rain, flash flooding, and embedded thunderstorms to southern New England from the morning to mid evening. In addition to much tree damage from straight line winds, there was one tornado in Connecticut, 2 in Rhode Island, and 1 in Massachusetts. These all occurred in the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An EF-0 with maximum winds of 75 mph briefly touched down in a|rural area of North Attleborough on Ellis Road which caused tree|damage south of High Street. The tree damage was limited to the|tops of three trees having been twisted off and lofted into nearby|pasture. After speaking with the homeowners they described seeing|the sheets of rain change direction before seeking shelter in|their basement. The tree damage along the path was consistent with|wind speeds between 65 and 75 mph, resulting an EF-0 rating on |the Enhanced Fujita Scale.

event_description: Governor Healey Issues Emergency Declaration, Activates National Guard Ahead of Hurricane Lee
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hurricane Lee passed east of Southern New England during the morning hours moving toward maritime Canada by midday. As it passed by it produced some tropical storm level sustained winds and wind gusts but impact was minimal. There were some downed trees and power lines and the maximum wind gust was 62 mph on the bay side of Cape Cod.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Provincetown, a tree branch was down blocking Standish St. Winds were generally gusting 40-50 mph.
